newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS -- Issues to watch - June 26.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS -- Issues to watch - June 26.

text.p: -- Komag Inc said results for its second quarter and the rest of its fiscal year would fall short of expectations due to weak demand for its disk drives.

The company said it expects second quarter earnings to be less than the first quarter's $0.33 per share. The First Call second quarter consensus earnings estimate is $0.45 per share. Komag last traded at 23-9/16 on Wednesday.

-- French drugs and chemical group Rhone-Poulenc said it was considering launching a $4.3 billion bid to buy the outstanding shares of Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc, in which it now holds a 68.3 percent stake. Rhone-Poulenc Rorer's stock closed in New York at 79-7/16.

-- Boeing Co, in its push to reach record production levels, is finding shortages of thousands of aircraft parts and delays in some planes, the Wall Street Journal reported. Boeing closed at 54-11/16.

-- Russell Corp said its second quarter earnings could be 50 percent below analysts' estimates and record year-earlier results. The company said most of the shortfall was the result of problems in its licensed products business. Its stock closed at 69-3/16.
